scenes.title: Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature
scenes.provenance: Rendered from the ECCO2 ocean model by NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio. Values here are estimated from pixel colour.
scenes.description: A flat map of the whole Earth, with the oceans filled by thin, moving flow lines that trace surface currents computed by the ECCO2 ocean model between 25 March 2007 and 3 March 2008. Each flow line is coloured by sea surface temperature: blue near 0 °C, green between about 10 and 20 °C, yellow near 25 °C and red near 32 °C. Land is shown in grey and carries no data. Red and yellow water fills the tropics. Along the western edges of the ocean basins, such as the Gulf Stream off North America and the Kuroshio off Japan, warm water is drawn poleward in narrow, fast currents and curls into eddies where it meets colder water. Near Antarctica and in the far North Atlantic the lines turn blue.
scenes.story: Warm water is carried poleward along the western edges of ocean basins. Sharp fronts appear where it meets cold water.

scenes.title: Lightning Events Detected from the International Space Station (ISS) 2017-2023
scenes.provenance: Lightning detected by the Lightning Imaging Sensor on the ISS, rendered by NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio. Events here are estimated from pixel colour.
scenes.description: A flat map of the Earth in shades of grey, covering 2017 to July 2023. Yellow and orange dots show where the Lightning Imaging Sensor on the International Space Station detected lightning. The picture uses a roving 10-day window, so each dot is part of a 10-day accumulation, not one flash at that instant. Coverage is limited to the latitudes the space station passes over, roughly 52 degrees north to 52 degrees south, so the far north and south stay empty. The dots cluster over tropical land: central Africa, South America, the Maritime Continent and South Asia. Through each year the band of activity drifts north during the northern summer and south during the southern summer.
scenes.story: Lightning concentrates over tropical land. Through the year the activity follows the summer hemisphere north and south.

scenes.title: GEOS Aerosols (2025)
scenes.tagline: Scan the air from west to east
scenes.provenance: Modelled by the GEOS Forward Processing system and rendered by NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio. Classes here are estimated from pixel colour.
scenes.description: A flat map of the whole Earth, stretched to a wide 16:9 frame, showing aerosols modelled by NASA's GEOS Forward Processing system for 19 August 2025 at 20:00 UTC. Four kinds of particle are drawn in different colours over a dark background. Black carbon and smoke appear red-orange, dust appears lilac to magenta, sea salt appears grey-teal to blue, and sulfate appears green. Sea salt spreads over the windy oceans, and Hurricane Erin stands out as a swirl in the sea-salt field in the western Atlantic. Dust from the Sahara streams west across the Atlantic. Smoke rises from fires in Africa and Spain. Sulfate appears near volcanoes such as Kilauea and Etna. Values are a model rendering, not observations at a single point.
scenes.story: Sea salt rises over windy oceans, Saharan dust crosses the Atlantic, and smoke drifts from fires in Africa and Spain. Sulfate marks volcanoes such as Kilauea and Etna, and Hurricane Erin stands out in the sea-salt field.
